items.name: Monic polynomials ordered by height
items.statement: V_n(Z) is the set of monic integer polynomials f(x) = x^n + a_1x^{n−1} + ⋯ + a_n of degree n (and V_n(R), V_n(Z_p) the real and p-adic analogues). The height is H(f) = max{|a_1|, |a_2|^{1/2}, …, |a_n|^{1/n}}, and #{f ∈ V_n(Z) : H(f) < X} = 2^nX^{n(n+1)/2} + O(X^{n(n+1)/2−1}). For S ⊂ V_n(Z), S_X is the set of elements of S of height < X. Volumes on V_n(Z_p) (resp. V_n(R)) are normalised so that V_n(Z_p) has volume 1 (resp. V_n(Z) has covolume 1).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The discriminant of a polynomial
items.statement: Δ(f) is the discriminant of f, equal up to sign to the resultant Res(f, f′), a polynomial with integer coefficients in a_1, …, a_n.
items.locator: §1, p.1; proof of Proposition 2.2, p.9, arXiv:1611.09806v3
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Resultant/Basic.lean:930 at 082e2d3 (the Sylvester-matrix definition, with the sign that makes real-rooted polynomials have non-negative discriminant).

items.name: Yamamura's density λ_n(p) of p² ∤ Δ
items.statement: For p ≠ 2 let λ_1(p) = 1, λ_2(p) = 1 − 1/p², and λ_n(p) = 1 − (3p^{n−1} − p^{n−2} + (−1)^n(p − 1)²)/(p^n(p + 1)) for n ≥ 3; let λ_1(2) = 1 and λ_n(2) = 1/2 for n ≥ 2. Then λ_n(p) is the density of monic f ∈ V_n(Z_p) with p² ∤ Δ(f) (Yamamura [26, Proposition 3]).
items.note: Checked by exhaustive count modulo p² for n ≤ 5 and p ∈ {2, 3, 5} whenever p^{2n} ≤ 2·10⁶ (for example λ_4(5) = 564/625). Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The constants λ_n and their limit λ
items.statement: λ_n := ∏_p λ_n(p) > 0, and λ_n → λ = (1/2)·∏_{p≥3}(1 − (3p − 1)/(p²(p + 1))) ≈ 30.7056% as n → ∞ (2). So as the degree grows, the probability that a random monic integer polynomial has squarefree discriminant tends to λ.
items.note: Computed with PARI: λ = 0.3070556828588…; λ_3, …, λ_8 ≈ 0.3426, 0.2997, 0.3091, 0.3064, 0.3072, 0.3070. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Lenstra's density ρ_n(p) = 1 − 1/p² of p-maximality
items.statement: For n > 1 and every prime p, the density of monic f ∈ V_n(Z_p) such that Z_p[x]/(f(x)) is the maximal order of Q_p[x]/(f(x)) is ρ_n(p) = 1 − 1/p², independently of n (H. W. Lenstra; [1, Proposition 3.5]). Hence ∏_pρ_n(p) = ζ(2)^{−1} ≈ 60.7927%.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: A squarefree discriminant forces maximality
items.statement: If the discriminant of an order Z[θ] in a number field is squarefree, the order is maximal: Δ(minpoly θ) = [O_K : Z[θ]]²·disc(K). Hence the irreducible polynomials counted in Theorem 1.1 are among those counted in Theorem 1.2.
items.note: The index formula; the squarefree corollary is one line from it (compare not_dvd_index_of_not_dvd_discr_minpoly, same file, line 118).

items.name: Squarefree discriminant implies Galois group S_n
items.statement: If f is a monic irreducible integer polynomial of degree n with squarefree discriminant, then the Galois group of its splitting field is S_n (see [20], [25], [16], [15]). Equivalently, a degree-n number field with squarefree discriminant has associated Galois group S_n.
items.note: Proof idea: the inertia groups are generated by transpositions and generate a normal transitive subgroup. Not in the atlas: PolynomialGaloisGroups Layer 3 treats the discriminant and A_n only. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Monogenic number fields
items.statement: A number field K is monogenic if Z[θ] = O_K for some θ ∈ K.
items.note: Tau Ceti also has isMonogenic_iff_exists_index_eq_one (same file).

items.name: The absolute discriminant of a number field
items.statement: The discriminant of K is the discriminant of O_K; Corollaries 1.3 and 1.4 count fields by its absolute value.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Discriminant/Defs.lean:36 at 082e2d3.

items.name: Hilbert irreducibility for monic polynomials by height
items.statement: A density of 100% of monic integer polynomials of degree n, ordered by H, are irreducible over Q and have Galois group S_n (Hilbert's irreducibility theorem). Consequently it does not matter whether irreducibility is imposed in Theorems 1.1–1.2.
items.note: IG.2 plans Hilbert irreducibility with specialization of regular covers. The power-saving form used in the proofs is Proposition 4.3.

items.name: Strong and weak divisibility of the discriminant by p²
items.statement: For a prime p and monic f ∈ V_n(Z) with p² | Δ(f), p² strongly divides Δ(f) if p² | Δ(f + pg) for every integer polynomial g of degree less than n (the paper says "of degree n"; since the leading coefficient of f + pg is then a p-adic unit, the two readings agree); otherwise p² weakly divides Δ(f).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Root-theoretic criterion for strong and weak divisibility (p odd)
items.statement: Let p be an odd prime and p² | Δ(f). Then p² strongly divides Δ(f) if and only if f mod p has at least two distinct multiple roots in F̄_p or a root in F_p of multiplicity ≥ 3; p² weakly divides Δ(f) if and only if f mod p has exactly one multiple root in F̄_p and it is a double root in F_p. For p = 2 every divisibility 4 | Δ(f) is strong (Stickelberger: Δ(f) ≡ 0 or 1 mod 4 for every lift), so W^{(2)}_m = ∅ for even m. The implication "two multiple roots or a triple root ⇒ strong" holds for every p, and it is the one used in Proposition 2.2.
items.locator: §1, p.4, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (error E1: stated for all p)
items.note: Checked by brute force over all f mod p for n ≤ 5, p ∈ {3, 5} (no exceptions), and p = 2, n = 2, …, 5 (failures, e.g. x² + 1 ≡ (x + 1)²). Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Collections of local specifications and κ-acceptability
items.statement: A collection of local specifications is Σ = (Σ_v)_v with Σ_p ⊂ V_n(Z_p) defined by congruence conditions modulo some power of p, and Σ_∞ ⊂ V_n(R) the degree-n polynomials whose number of real roots lies in a fixed nonempty subset of {0, …, n}. V(Σ) is the set of f ∈ V_n(Z) with f ∈ Σ_v for all v. Σ is κ-acceptable if every Σ_p is defined modulo p^κ and, for all sufficiently large p, Σ_p contains every f ∈ V_n(Z_p) with p² ∤ Δ(f). The specifications of Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 are 2-acceptable.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 2.2 (the shape of a weakly divisible polynomial)
items.statement: Let m be a positive squarefree integer and f a monic integer polynomial whose discriminant is weakly divisible by p² for all p | m. Then there is an integer ℓ with f(x + ℓ) = x^n + b_1x^{n−1} + ⋯ + b_{n−1}x + b_n, m | b_{n−1} and m² | b_n (9). The proof reduces to m = p by CRT, moves the double root to 0, and uses the identity Δ(f) = b_nΔ_1 + b_{n−1}²Δ_3 with Δ_1 ∈ Z[b_1, …, b_n], Δ_3 ∈ Z[b_1, …, b_{n−1}] (10), obtained from the Sylvester matrix of Res(f, f′). The integer ℓ is unique mod m.
items.locator: Proposition 2.2 and proof, pp.8–9; remark after Theorem 2.3, p.10, arXiv:1611.09806v3
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The representation of SO_n on symmetric matrices
items.statement: A_0 is the n × n symmetric matrix with 1s on the anti-diagonal. G = SO(A_0) (n = 2g + 1) or G = SO(A_0)/μ_2 = PSO_n (n = 2g + 2) acts on the space W of symmetric n × n matrices by γ·B = γBγ^t. The invariant polynomial of B is f_B(x) = (−1)^{n(n−1)/2}det(A_0x − B), a monic polynomial of degree n (the sign is (−1)^g for n odd and (−1)^{g+1} for n even). Δ(B) := Δ(f_B) and H(B) := H(f_B). (1/2)W(Z) and (1/4)W(Z) are the lattices of B with coefficient denominators dividing 2 and 4.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The invariant ring of W
items.statement: The ring of polynomial invariants for the action of G(C) on W(C) is freely generated by the coefficients of the invariant polynomial f_B(x) ([3, §4]; for n even, [23, §2.1–2.2]).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Stabilizers are the 2-torsion of the Jacobian
items.statement: Let k have characteristic ≠ 2 and f ∈ k[x] monic of degree n with Δ(f) ≠ 0; C_f : y² = f(x) is the smooth hyperelliptic curve of genus g, with one rational Weierstrass point at infinity (n odd) or two rational non-Weierstrass points at infinity (n even), and J_f is its Jacobian. The stabilizer in G(k) of any B ∈ W(k) with f_B = f is naturally isomorphic to J_f[2](k), so has order ≤ #J_f[2](k̄) = 2^{2g} ([4, Proposition 5.1] for n odd; [24, Proposition 2.33] for n even).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Distinguished elements and orbits
items.statement: B ∈ W(k) with Δ(B) ≠ 0 is k-distinguished if, for n = 2g + 1, there is a g-dimensional subspace over k isotropic for both A_0 and B; for n = 2g + 2, if there is a flag Y′ ⊂ Y over k with Y (g + 1)-dimensional isotropic for A_0 and Y′ g-dimensional isotropic for B. W^dist ⊂ W(Q) is the set of Q-distinguished elements. The distinguished G(Q)-orbits correspond to the identity 2-Selmer elements of J_f.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Isotropic subspaces of a distinguished element
items.statement: If B is k-distinguished, the set of g-dimensional k-subspaces isotropic for A_0 and B (n odd), resp. of the flags of the definition (n even), is in bijection with J_f[2](k), so has at most 2^{2g} elements ([4, Proposition 4.1]; [24, Proposition 2.32]).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: J_f[2](k) and factorizations of f
items.statement: For n odd, J_f[2](k) is in natural bijection with the even-degree factors of f over k ([4, Proposition 5.1]); for n even, with the even-degree factorizations of f over k ([5, Proposition 22]). Over k̄ there are 2^{2g} of them. In particular J_f[2](k) is trivial if f is irreducible over k and, for n even, does not factor as g(x)ḡ(x) over a quadratic extension of k.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The subspace W_0 and its parabolic G_0
items.statement: For n = 2g + 1, W_0 ⊂ W is the subspace of B whose top left g × g block is 0, and G_0 ⊂ G is the subgroup of γ such that γ^t preserves the span Y_g of the first g basis vectors; γ ∈ G_0 has block form (γ_1 0; δ γ_2) (5) and acts on the top right g × (g + 1) block by (γ·B)^top = γ_1B^topγ_2^t. For n = 2g + 2, W_0 is the subspace of B whose top left g × (g + 1) block is 0, and G_0 is the parabolic subgroup of γ with γ^t preserving the flag Y_g ⊂ Y_{g+1}; γ has the block form (24) with blocks γ_1, α, γ_2 and again (γ·B)^top = γ_1B^topγ_2^t. Elements of W_0(k) with nonzero discriminant are k-distinguished.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The Q-invariant of 2 ⊗ g ⊗ (g + 1)
items.statement: Write v ∈ V_g = 2 ⊗ g ⊗ (g + 1) as a pair (A, B) of g × (g + 1) matrices, a representation of H_g = SL_2 × GL_g × GL_{g+1}. Let M_v(x, y) be the vector whose i-th coordinate is (−1)^{i−1} times the g × g minor of Ax − By omitting the i-th column; these are g + 1 binary forms of degree g. Q(v) is the determinant of the (g + 1) × (g + 1) matrix of their coefficients. It is a relative invariant: Q((γ_0, γ_1, γ_2)·v) = det(γ_1)^{g+1}det(γ_2)^gQ(v) (6), invariant under SL_2 × SL_g × SL_{g+1}. By SL_2-invariance it is homogeneous of degree g(g + 1)/2 in B.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The Q-invariant on W_0
items.statement: For B ∈ W_0 put Q(B) := Q(A_0^top, B^top), using the top right g × (g + 1) blocks ((7), (25)). It is a relative invariant of G_0: Q(γ·B) = det(γ_1)Q(B) for n odd (8), and Q(γ·B) = det(γ_1)^{g+1}det(γ_2)^gQ(B) = det(γ_1)α^{−g}Q(B) for n even (26).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Q² divides the discriminant on W_0
items.statement: As polynomials in the coordinates of W_0, the discriminant Δ is divisible by Q². So Δ restricted to W_0 is not squarefree and the Ekedahl sieve does not apply to it; moreover σ_m(f), viewed in (1/2)W_0(Z), has discriminant strongly divisible by p² for every p | m, even though Δ(f) is only weakly divisible.
items.locator: §1, p.5; remark after Theorem 2.3, p.10, arXiv:1611.09806v3
items.note: Asserted "as we will show in the sequel" but not proved in the paper. Q² | Δ was checked at 53–60 random points of W_0(Z) for each n = 3, …, 7. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 2.1 (|Q| is well defined, n odd)
items.statement: Let n = 2g + 1 and B ∈ W_0(Q) with f_B irreducible over Q. Then Q(B′) = ±Q(B) for every B′ ∈ W_0(Q) that is G(Z)-equivalent to B. Proof: Y_g and γ^tY_g are both isotropic for A_0 and B, and J_f[2](Q) is trivial, so γ ∈ G_0(Z), and (8) applies.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 3.1 (|Q| is well defined, n even)
items.statement: Let n = 2g + 2 and B ∈ W_0(Q) with f_B irreducible over Q and, when n ≥ 4, not of the form g(x)ḡ(x) over a quadratic extension of Q. Then Q(B′) = ±Q(B) for every B′ ∈ W_0(Q) that is G(Z)-equivalent to B.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The |Q|-invariant and the sets L
items.statement: For B ∈ W(Q) that is G(Z)-equivalent to some B′ ∈ W_0(Q), with f_B irreducible (and, for n even, not g(x)ḡ(x) over a quadratic field), |Q|(B) := |Q(B′)|, independent of B′ by Propositions 2.1 and 3.1. L is the set of v ∈ (1/2)W(Z) (n odd), resp. v ∈ (1/4)W(Z) (n even), that are G(Z)-equivalent to an element of (1/2)W_0(Z), resp. (1/4)W_0(Z), with f_v satisfying these conditions; L ⊂ W^dist. N(L; M; X) is the number of G(Z)-classes in L with |Q| > M and height < X.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The matrices B_m(c_1, …, c_n) for odd n (11)
items.statement: For n = 2g + 1 and integers m, c_1, …, c_n, B_m ∈ (1/2)W_0(Z) is the symmetric matrix with b_{1,n−1} = b_{n−1,1} = m, b_{i,n−i} = 1 for 2 ≤ i ≤ n − 2, whose lower right (g + 1) × (g + 1) block (rows and columns g + 1, …, n) is tridiagonal with diagonal −c_1, −c_3, …, −c_n and off-diagonal entries −c_2/2, −c_4/2, …, −c_{n−1}/2, and whose other entries are 0. Then f_{B_m}(x) = x^n + c_1x^{n−1} + ⋯ + c_{n−2}x² + mc_{n−1}x + m²c_n and Q(B_m) = ±m, and for every integer ℓ, f_{B+ℓA_0}(x) = f_B(x − ℓ) (12) and Q(B + ℓA_0) = Q(B) (13).
items.note: Verified symbolically for g = 1, 2, 3. With the minor-sign convention of p.7, Q(B_m) = m for g = 1, 3 and −m for g = 2 (the ordering of the coefficient matrix is not fixed; only |Q| is used). Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 2.3 (the embedding σ_m, n odd)
items.statement: Let n be odd and m a positive squarefree integer. There is a map σ_m : W^{(2)}_m → (1/2)W_0(Z) with f_{σ_m(f)} = f and Q(σ_m(f)) = m (14), namely σ_m(f) = B_m(c_1, …, c_n) + ℓA_0 where f(x + ℓ) = x^n + c_1x^{n−1} + ⋯ + mc_{n−1}x + m²c_n (Proposition 2.2). No two elements of the image are G(C)-equivalent.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 2.4 (orbits of |Q|-invariant m, n odd)
items.statement: Let W^{(2),irr}_m be the irreducible polynomials in W^{(2)}_m. There is an injective map σ̄_m : W^{(2),irr}_m → G(Z)\L with f_{σ̄_m(f)} = f, and every B in an orbit in the image has |Q|(B) = m. Hence the left side of Theorem 1.5(b), up to reducible polynomials, is at most N(L; M; X).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The matrices B_m(c_1, …, c_n) for even n (27)
items.statement: For n = 2g + 2 and integers m, c_1, …, c_n, B_m ∈ (1/4)W_0(Z) is the symmetric matrix with b_{1,n−1} = b_{n−1,1} = m, b_{i,n−i} = 1 for 2 ≤ i ≤ n − 2, b_{g+1,g+2} = b_{g+2,g+1} = −c_1/2, whose lower right (g + 1) × (g + 1) block (rows and columns g + 2, …, n) is tridiagonal with diagonal c_1²/4 − c_2, −c_4, −c_6, …, −c_n and off-diagonal entries −c_3/2, −c_5/2, …, −c_{n−1}/2, and whose other entries are 0. Then f_{B_m}(x) = x^n + c_1x^{n−1} + ⋯ + c_{n−2}x² + mc_{n−1}x + m²c_n and Q(B_m) = ±m.
items.note: Verified symbolically for g = 1, 2, 3 (Q = m for g = 1, 3, −m for g = 2). Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 3.2 (the embedding σ_m, n even)
items.statement: Let n be even and m a positive squarefree integer. There is a map σ_m : W^{(2)}_m → (1/4)W(Z), with image in (1/4)W_0(Z), such that f_{σ_m(f)} = f and Q(σ_m(f)) = m (28), namely σ_m(f) = B_m(c_1, …, c_n) + ℓA_0.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 3.3 (orbits of |Q|-invariant m, n even)
items.statement: Let W^{(2),irr}_m be the polynomials in W^{(2)}_m that are irreducible over Q and do not factor as g(x)ḡ(x) over any quadratic extension of Q. There is an injective map σ̄_m : W^{(2),irr}_m → G(Z)\L with f_{σ̄_m(f)} = f for every f ∈ W^{(2),irr}_m, and every element of every orbit in the image has |Q|-invariant m.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.0/ST.1 as a source.

items.name: The tail sets W^{(1)}_m, W^{(2)}_m and W_m
items.statement: For squarefree m > 0, W^{(1)}_m (resp. W^{(2)}_m) is the set of f ∈ V_n(Z) whose discriminant is strongly (resp. weakly) divisible by p² for every prime p | m; W_m is the set of f ∈ V_n(Z) with m² | Δ(f); a subscript X restricts to height < X.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Iwasawa decomposition and a Siegel-set fundamental set
items.statement: G(R) = N(R)TK with N the lower-triangular unipotent group, T the split torus and K compact, and a fundamental set F for the left action of G(Z) on G(R) can be taken inside a Siegel set N′T′K, with N′ absolutely bounded and T′ = {(s) : s_i ≥ c}.
items.note: AA.3 plans Siegel sets, their height estimates and the finite covering of arithmetic quotients.

items.name: Reduction to an integral over the torus (odd n)
items.statement: Let n = 2g + 1, R a bounded fundamental domain for G(R) on {B ∈ W(R) : Δ(B) ≠ 0, H(B) < 1} ([4, §9.1]), and G_1 ⊂ G(R) a compact left K-invariant set that is the closure of a nonempty open set. Since (Fh)·(XR) covers a fundamental domain at most 2^{2g} times, N(L; M; X) ≪ #{B ∈ (Fh)·(XR) ∩ L : |Q|(B) > M} (15); averaging over h ∈ G_1 gives (16), and with the Haar measure dγ = dn δ(s)d^×s dk, δ(s) = ∏_{k=1}^g s_k^{k²−2kg} (17), s_i = t_i/t_{i+1} (i < g), s_g = t_g, and the bounded set E = N″KG_1R, N(L; M; X) ≪ ∫_{s_i≫1}#{B ∈ ((s)·XE) ∩ L : |Q|(B) > M}δ(s)d^×s (18).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Reduction to an integral over the torus (even n)
items.statement: Let n = 2g + 2, with R and F as in [23, §4.1], s_i = t_i/t_{i+1} for 1 ≤ i ≤ g and s_{g+1} = t_gt_{g+1}, d^×s = ∏_{i=1}^{g+1}ds_i/s_i, and δ(s) = ∏_{k=1}^{g−1}s_k^{k²−2kg−k}·(s_gs_{g+1})^{−g(g+1)/2} (30). Then N(L; M; X) ≪ ∫_{γ∈F}#{B ∈ ((γG_1)·(XR)) ∩ L : |Q|(B) > M}dγ (29) and N(L; M; X) ≪ ∫_{s_i≫1}#{B ∈ ((s)·XE) ∩ L : |Q|(B) > M}δ(s)d^×s (31), with E = N″KG_1R bounded.
items.note: δ(s) is the modular character of the D_{g+1} root system in these coordinates, checked against 2ρ. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Torus weights of the coordinates and of Q (odd n)
items.note: Checked symbolically for g ≤ 5. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Torus weights of the coordinates and of Q (even n)
items.statement: For n = 2g + 2 and T = diag(t_1^{−1}, …, t_{g+1}^{−1}, t_{g+1}, …, t_1), the weight of b_ij is t_i^{−1}t_j^{−1} (i, j ≤ g + 1), t_i^{−1}t_{n−j+1} (i ≤ g + 1 < j), t_{n−i+1}t_{n−j+1} (i, j > g + 1) (32), and w(Q) = (t_1⋯t_g)^{−1}t_{g+1}^g = ∏_{k=1}^gs_k^{−k} (36, corrected). Every entry of B ∈ (s)·XE is ≪ Xw(b_ij), and |Q(B)| ≪ X^{g(g+1)/2}w(Q).
items.note: Checked symbolically for g ≤ 5: with s_{g+1} = t_gt_{g+1}, (t_1⋯t_g)^{−1}t_{g+1}^g = ∏s_k^{−k}, as the proof of Proposition 3.6 uses. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 2.5 (most distinguished points lie in W_00, odd n)
items.statement: Let W_00 ⊂ W be the symmetric matrices with b_ij = 0 whenever i + j < n. Then ∫_{s_i≫1}#{B ∈ ((s)·XE) ∩ ((1/2)W(Z) ∖ (1/2)W_00(Z)) : b_11 = 0}δ(s)d^×s = O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2−1+ε}) (20) and ∫_{s_i≫1}#{B ∈ ((s)·XE) ∩ L : b_11 ≠ 0}δ(s)d^×s = o(X^{n(n+1)/2}) (21) ([4, Propositions 10.5 and 10.7]).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Distinguished elements have p-adic density bounded away from 1
items.statement: The p-adic density of Q_p-distinguished elements of W(Z_p) is bounded uniformly away from 1: for n = 2g + 1 it is at most 1 − g/(2g + 1) + O(1/p) ([4, §10.7]); for n even this is shown in the proof of [23, Proposition 23].
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 2.6, p.13; proof of Proposition 3.5, p.19, citing [4], [23], arXiv:1611.09806v3
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: The Selberg-sieve step of Shankar–Tsimerman
items.statement: If the local densities of a set of lattice points defined by conditions at each p are bounded uniformly away from 1, the Selberg sieve applied to the count of (s)·XE-points with b_11 ≠ 0, exactly as in [22], saves a power: the count is O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2−1/5+ε}).
items.locator: Proofs of Propositions 2.6 and 3.5, pp.13, 19, citing [22], arXiv:1611.09806v3
items.note: Stated only by reference to [22]; the exponent 1/5 is inherited from there. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: The Selberg upper-bound sieve
items.statement: The Λ²-sieve: for a sifted set with local densities, the Selberg weights give an upper bound for the number of elements avoiding the excluded residue classes, with the main term governed by the local densities and an error from the level of distribution.
items.locator: Proofs of Propositions 2.6 and 3.5, pp.13, 19, arXiv:1611.09806v3
items.note: Mathlib 082e2d3 has the Λ² upper-bound mechanism: NumberTheory/SelbergSieve.lean, SelbergSieve.siftedSum_le_mainSum_errSum_of_upperMoebius (line 216), upperMoebius_lambdaSquared (line 250) and the main-term diagonalisation (line 375). SV.1, as narrowed by RS-07, plans the optimisation of the Selberg main term beyond that diagonalisation, which the application needs.

items.name: Proposition 2.6 (power saving off W_00, odd n)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 2.7 (large |Q| in the cusp, odd n)
items.statement: ∫_{s_i≫1}#{B ∈ ((s)·XE) ∩ L ∩ (1/2)W_00(Z) : |Q|(B) > M}δ(s)d^×s = O(X^{n(n+1)/2}log X/M). Proof: an element of (1/2)W_00(Z) with a zero entry b_{i,n−i} has discriminant 0, and w(b_{i,n−i}) = s_i^{−1}, so only 1 ≪ s_i ≪ X matters; there the lattice points number ≪ ∏_{α∈S}Xw(α) = X^{n(n+1)/2−g²}∏_ks_k^{2k−1}·δ(s)^{−1} (S the coordinates of W_00), and X^{g(g+1)/2}w(Q) ≫ M gives the factor 1/M; the integrand becomes X^{n(n+1)/2−g(g−1)/2}∏s_k^{k−1}, and the log X comes from s_1.
items.note: The exponent chain was checked symbolically for g ≤ 5, and the vanishing of Δ when some b_{i,n−i} = 0 in W_00 was tested for n = 3, …, 7. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 3.6 (large |Q| in the cusp, even n)
items.statement: ∫_{s_i≫1}#{B ∈ ((s)·XE) ∩ L ∩ (1/4)W_00(Z) : |Q|(B) > M}δ(s)d^×s = O(X^{n(n+1)/2}log²X/M). Nonemptiness forces Xs_i^{−1} ≫ 1, Xs_gs_{g+1}^{−1} ≫ 1 and X^{g(g+1)/2}w(Q) ≫ M (37); the integrand is X^{n(n+1)/2−g(g+1)}∏_{k≤g−1}s_k^{2k−1}·s_g^{g−1}s_{g+1}^g, and after the factors 1/M and (Xs_gs_{g+1}^{−1})^g ≫ 1 it becomes X^{n(n+1)/2−g(g+1)/2+g}∏_{k≤g−1}s_k^{k−1}·s_g^{g−1}; the log²X comes from s_1 and s_{g+1}.
items.locator: Proposition 3.6 and proof, pp.19–20, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (misprints E3, E4)

items.name: Bhargava's quantitative Ekedahl sieve ([2, Theorem 3.3]) in weighted form
items.statement: Let Y ⊂ A^n_Z be a closed subscheme of codimension k ≥ 2 and B ⊂ R^n a bounded region with a reasonable boundary. Then #{a ∈ rB ∩ Z^n : a mod p ∈ Y(F_p) for some prime p > M} = O(r^n/(M^{k−1}log M) + r^{n−k+1}). The same proof applies to weighted homogeneous expansions and to a union over squarefree m > M of the conditions at all p | m; for the codimension-2 locus of polynomials with two multiple roots or a triple root it gives Theorem 1.5(a), with the smaller second error term O(X^{n(n+1)/2−1}) because a_n has the largest range.
items.note: The adaptation is asserted, not written out. The same external theorem is routed to ST.2 by PAPER-KOYMANS-MILOVIC-21. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 1.5(a) (tail estimate, strongly divisible case)
items.statement: For every M > 0 and ε > 0, #⋃_{m>M, m squarefree}{f ∈ W^{(1)}_m : H(f) < X} = O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2+ε}/M) + O(X^{n(n+1)/2−1}), with implied constants independent of M and X.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 1.5(b) (tail estimate, weakly divisible case)
items.statement: For every M > 0 and ε > 0, #⋃_{m>M, m squarefree}{f ∈ W^{(2)}_m : H(f) < X} = O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2+ε}/M) + O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2−1/5+ε}), with implied constants independent of M and X. For odd n it follows from Theorem 2.4 and Propositions 2.5–2.7, for even n from Theorem 3.3 and Propositions 3.4–3.6, together with Proposition 4.3.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 4.2 (polynomials with a rational root)
items.statement: The number of f ∈ V_n(Z)_X with a rational linear factor is O(X^{n(n+1)/2−n+1}log X). Proof: a_n = 0 gives O(X^{n(n+1)/2−n}); otherwise count (a_1, …, a_{n−2}, a_n, r) with r | a_n, which determines a_{n−1}, using Σ_{|a_n|≤X^n}d(a_n) ≪ X^nlog X.
items.locator: Lemma 4.2 and proof, p.21, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (gap E8)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Dietmann's quantitative Hilbert irreducibility ([7, Lemma 2, Lemma 4, Theorem 1])
items.statement: x^n + a_1x^{n−1} + ⋯ + a_{n−1}x + t has Galois group S_n over Q(t) for all (a_1, …, a_{n−1}) with |a_i| ≤ X^i outside a set of O(X^{(n−1)(n−2)/2}) tuples ([7, Lemma 2]). For such a tuple and H ⊂ S_n, the number of integers t with |t| ≤ T for which the specialization has Galois group H over Q is O_ε(T^{1/[S_n:H]+ε}) ([7, Theorem 1]). The Galois group of a reducible polynomial without a rational root has index ≥ n(n − 1)/2 in S_n ([7, Lemma 4]).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.3, p.22, citing [7], arXiv:1611.09806v3
items.note: Routed to InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.2 as a source.

items.name: Proposition 4.3 (reducible polynomials are negligible)
items.statement: Let V_n(Z)^red be the polynomials that are reducible or, for n ≥ 4, factor as g(x)ḡ(x) over a quadratic extension of Q. Then #V_n(Z)^red_X = O(X^{n(n+1)/2−n+1}log X). Proof: Lemma 4.2, Dietmann's bounds with T = X^n, and index bounds for the possible Galois groups. The argument as written establishes this for n ≠ 4; for n = 4 it gives O_ε(X^{22/3+ε}) (E7). Every application needs only O(X^{n(n+1)/2−1/5}).
items.locator: Proposition 4.3 and proof, pp.21–22, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (error E7)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 4.4 (uniformity for m² | Δ)
items.statement: For every M > 0, Σ_{m>M, m squarefree}#W_{m,X} = O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2+ε}/√M) + O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2−1/5+ε}) (39). Proof: f lies in O(X^ε) sets W_m; with k_1 (resp. k_2) the product of the primes p for which p² strongly (resp. weakly) divides Δ(f), f ∈ W^{(1)}_{k_1} ∩ W^{(2)}_{k_2} with k_1k_2 > M, so k_1 > √M or k_2 > √M, and Theorem 1.5 applies.
items.locator: Theorem 4.4 and proof, pp.22–23, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (misprint E5)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Remark after Theorem 4.4 (the denominator √M improves to M)
items.statement: The √M in (39) can be improved to M: split W_m into W^{(1)}_{m_1} ∩ W^{(2)}_{m_2} over dyadic ranges of m_1, m_2, embed W^{(2)}_{m_2} into (1/4)W(Z), and in the (1/4)W_00(Z) piece impose strong divisibility by p² for p | m_1 and apply the quantitative Ekedahl sieve, saving 1/m_1. This gives O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2+ε}/M) + O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2−1/5+ε}).
items.note: Outlined only. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 4.1 (the squarefree sieve with κ-acceptable conditions)
items.statement: Let κ ≥ 1 and Σ be κ-acceptable. Then #V(Σ)_X = Vol(Σ_{∞,H<1})∏_pVol(Σ_p)·X^{n(n+1)/2} + O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2−min{1/5,1/(2κ)}+ε}), where Σ_{∞,H<1} is the set of elements of Σ_∞ of height < 1, and the implied constant depends only on n and Σ. Proof: inclusion–exclusion #V(Σ)_X = Σ_mμ(m)#W_m(Σ)_X over squarefree m, with W_m(Σ) the f with f ∉ Σ_p for all p | m; lattice-point counts for m ≤ X^{1/κ}; and (40) with Theorem 4.4 for m > X^{1/κ}.
items.locator: Theorem 4.1, p.21; proof §4.2, (40)–(41), pp.22–23, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (error E6, misprint E5)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.2 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (density of squarefree discriminants)
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1. When monic integer polynomials f of degree n are ordered by H(f), the density of those with squarefree discriminant Δ(f) exists and equals λ_n = ∏_pλ_n(p) > 0.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Power-saving count of squarefree discriminants ((4), first line)
items.statement: For n > 1, #{f ∈ V_n(Z) : H(f) < X, Δ(f) squarefree} = λ_n·2^nX^{n(n+1)/2} + O_ε(X^{n(n+1)/2−1/5+ε}). Theorem 4.1 with κ = 2 gives it. Since reducible polynomials are fewer than the error term, irreducibility may be imposed.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 1.2 (density of monogenic maximal orders)
items.statement: Let n > 1. When monic integer polynomials f of degree n are ordered by H(f), the density of those for which Z[x]/(f(x)) is the ring of integers of its fraction field is ∏_p(1 − 1/p²) = ζ(2)^{−1}. Since 100% are irreducible with Galois group S_n, about 60.7927% of monic integer polynomials of degree n are irreducible with Z[x]/(f) maximal.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Power-saving count of maximal orders ((4), second line)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Signature and local-condition variants
items.statement: Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 remain true for polynomials with a prescribed number of real roots, and with any finite set of local conditions at finitely many places (with positive, easily computable constants) that do not force the counted set to be empty; certain infinite sets of local conditions are allowed (Theorem 4.1).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: The Ellenberg–Venkatesh upper bound ([9, Remark 3.3])
items.statement: The number of number fields K of degree n with s(K) ≤ Y is ≪ Y^{(n−1)(n+2)/2}, where s(K) = inf{‖x‖ : x ∈ O_K, Q(x) = K} and ‖x‖ is the maximum of the archimedean absolute values of x. A bound on ‖x‖ bounds the coefficients of the minimal polynomial; translating x by an integer removes one coefficient.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: The lattice R_g, quasi-reduced and strongly quasi-reduced polynomials
items.statement: For g ∈ V_n(R) with Δ(g) ≠ 0, with r real and 2s complex roots, R[x]/(g(x)) ≅ R^r × C^s ≅ R^n via the real and complex embeddings (C = R + R√−1). R_g is the lattice spanned by 1, θ, …, θ^{n−1}, θ the image of x; for g ∈ V_n(Z), R_g is the image of Z[x]/(g(x)). g is quasi-reduced if there are monic integer polynomials h_i of degree i (1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1) such that 1, h_1(θ), …, h_{n−1}(θ) is a Minkowski-reduced basis of R_g, and strongly quasi-reduced if moreover Z[x]/(g(x)) has a unique Minkowski-reduced basis (necessarily read up to the signs of the basis vectors).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 5.1 (corrected: strongly quasi-reduced polynomials give distinct rings up to x ↦ −x)
items.statement: Let g, g* be monic integer polynomials of degree n with nonzero discriminant, strongly quasi-reduced, with vanishing x^{n−1}-coefficients. If Z[x]/(g(x)) ≅ Z[x]/(g*(x)) as rings, then g*(x) = g(x) or g*(x) = (−1)^ng(−x). (The printed statement concludes g = g*, which fails for the pair g(x), (−1)^ng(−x); E10.)
items.locator: Lemma 5.1 and proof, p.24, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (error E10)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 5.2 (scaling makes a polynomial quasi-reduced)
items.statement: If g is a monic real polynomial with nonzero discriminant, then g(ρx) is quasi-reduced for all sufficiently large ρ > 0. Proof: the Gram matrix of 1, ρθ, …, ρ^{n−1}θ^{n−1} is ΛQ_1Λ^T with Λ = diag(1, ρ, …, ρ^{n−1}), so the torus part of its Iwasawa decomposition is (t_1, ρt_2, …, ρ^{n−1}t_n), whose successive ratios tend to infinity.
items.locator: Lemma 5.2 and proof, pp.24–25, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (gap E12)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Lemma 5.3 (100% are strongly quasi-reduced)
items.statement: A density of 100% of irreducible monic integer polynomials of degree n, ordered by H, are strongly quasi-reduced. Proof: choose a compact B of real polynomials of height < 1 with volume > (1 − ε) of the whole, take ρ_B with f(ρx) quasi-reduced for all f ∈ B and ρ > ρ_B (continuity of ρ_f), and count integer points in ρ·B, where H(ρ·f) = ρH(f).
items.locator: Lemma 5.3 and proof, p.25, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (gap E12)
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Theorem 5.4 (squarefree discriminants with a_1 = 0 or 0 ≤ a_1 < n)
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1. When monic integer polynomials with a_1 = 0 are ordered by H, the density with squarefree Δ(f) exists and equals κ_n = ∏_pκ_n(p) > 0, where κ_n(p) is the density of monic f over Z_p with vanishing x^{n−1}-coefficient and p² ∤ Δ(f). With 0 ≤ a_1 < n in place of a_1 = 0 the density is λ_n. The proof of Theorem 1.1 goes through with W, W_0, W_00 replaced by the anti-trace-0 subspaces (as in [4], where the only difference is a factor of X in the counts).
items.locator: Theorem 5.4 and the following paragraph, pp.25–26; §2.3, p.11, arXiv:1611.09806v3
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Corollary 1.3 (monogenic S_n-fields)
items.statement: Let n > 1. The number of isomorphism classes of number fields of degree n and absolute discriminant less than X that are monogenic and have associated Galois group S_n is ≫ X^{1/2+1/n}. Proof: polynomials with a_1 = 0 of height < X^{1/(n(n−1))} have |Δ| ≪ X; by Theorem 5.4 and Lemma 5.3, ≫ X^{(2+3+⋯+n)/(n(n−1))} = X^{1/2+1/n} of them are strongly quasi-reduced with squarefree discriminant, and by Lemma 5.1 they give distinct fields (at most two polynomials per field, by the corrected Lemma 5.1).
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Remark 5.5 (signatures and local conditions in Corollary 1.3)
items.statement: Corollary 1.3 holds with prescribed real signature, and with any local conditions at a finite set of primes that do not contradict local monogeneity.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Corollary 1.4 (the Ellenberg–Venkatesh conjecture on short generating vectors)
items.statement: Let n > 1. The number of isomorphism classes of number fields K of degree n whose shortest vector in O_K generating K has length less than Y is ≍ Y^{(n−1)(n+2)/2}, and the same holds for fields whose normal closure has Galois group S_n. Proof of the lower bound: irreducible f = x^n + a_2x^{n−2} + ⋯ + a_n with H(f) ≤ Y have roots with ‖θ‖ ≪ Y (43); by Theorem 5.4 and Lemma 5.3, ≫ Y^{(n−1)(n+2)/2} of them are strongly quasi-reduced with squarefree discriminant, and Lemma 5.1 makes their fields distinct.
items.note: Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Remark 5.6 (conjectural asymptotic for monogenic fields)
items.statement: Conjecture: a positive proportion of monic integer polynomials of degree n with 0 ≤ a_1 < n and |Δ| < X have height O(X^{1/(n(n−1))}); and the number of monogenic number fields of degree n with absolute discriminant < X is asymptotic to (nC_n/(2ζ(2)))X^{1/2+1/n} (42), where C_n is the (n − 1)-dimensional volume of {f ∈ V_n(R) : a_1 = 0, |Δ(f)| < 1}. For n = 3, C_3 = 2^{1/3}(3 + √3)/45·Γ(1/2)Γ(1/6)/Γ(2/3).
items.note: A conjecture. C_3 was checked by direct integration of the area of {|4a_2³ + 27a_3²| < 1}: 0.96530936 against the printed closed form 0.965309365. Routed to ArithmeticStatistics ST.3/ST.5 as a source.

items.name: Minkowski-reduced bases and the Siegel-set description
items.statement: A Z-basis α_1, …, α_n of a lattice L is Minkowski-reduced if, successively for i = 1, …, n, α_i is a shortest vector of L such that α_1, …, α_i extends to a Z-basis of L; most lattices have a unique one (up to signs). For a positive definite form Q = γI_nγ^T with γ = ντκ (ν lower unipotent, τ = diag(t_1, …, t_n), κ ∈ SO_n(R)), Minkowski-reduced forms lie in a Siegel set F_SL = {ντκ : ν ∈ N′, t_i ≤ ct_{i+1}}.
items.locator: §5, footnote 1, p.24; proof of Lemma 5.2, p.25, arXiv:1611.09806v3 (gap E12)
items.note: Routed to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3 as a source.

items.name: Fujiwara's root bound (corrected)
items.statement: Every root θ of x^n + a_1x^{n−1} + ⋯ + a_n ∈ C[x] satisfies |θ| ≤ 2·max{|a_1|, |a_2|^{1/2}, …, |a_{n−1}|^{1/(n−1)}, |a_n/2|^{1/n}} (Fujiwara [10]). In particular H(f) ≤ Y implies ‖θ‖ ≪ Y.
items.note: Routed to ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.3 as a source.
